newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tanker leaks gas, 350 admitted to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Indian tanker leaks gas, 350 admitted to hospital.

text.p: At least 350 people with sore eyes caused by a gas leak from an overturned tanker were admitted to hospital in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh on Tuesday, police said.
Vijay David, a senior state police official said: "There were around 350 people who had reported at the district hospital with symptoms of burning sensations in their eyes."
No deaths had been reported so far and the victims were discharged after first-aid was administered to them, he added.

The leak occurred on a highway 75 km (47 miles) from the state capital Bhopal, when a tanker filled with ammonia gas got detached from the truck carrying it and fell into a 6.5-yard deep gorge, David said.
The gas engulfed a 500-metre (1,625 ft) area and caused a burning sensation in the eyes of villagers living nearby, a police spokesman said.
Bhopal is also the site of the world's worst industrial disaster 12 years ago.
On December 2, 1984, deadly gas which leaked from a pesticides plant owned by a unit of U.S.-based Union Carbide Corp engulfed Bhopal. Some 6,500 people were killed and at least 20,000 were injured.
